transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning smell from a tumble dryer is a serious fire risk. You must stop using the appliance immediately and unplug it from the wall. The most common cause is restricted airflow (a full lint filter or blocked vent) causing the heater to overheat, but it could also be an electrical fault. Because this involves potential fire damage and high-voltage components, you cannot safely diagnose or fix this yourself once a burning smell has appeared. Please do not attempt to run the machine again 'to see if it happens'. You need a qualified engineer to inspect the internal wiring, heater assembly, and airflow path before it can be considered safe. If you are comfortable doing so while it is unplugged, you can check that the lint filter is clean and the rear vent hose isn't crushed, but this will not make the machine safe to use until an engineer has confirmed there is no underlying damage.

plan: They asked: "is it safe to keep using it" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "giving off a burning smell". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
